db623a5ac56c35636f8e7e92a67e3aafa34a6f6d.summary: Elastic Security write-up on in-the-wild exploitation of four Microsoft Exchange Server zero-days (CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858, CVE-2021-27065) patched in March 2021. Microsoft attributed the initial activity to HAFNIUM; the report notes opportunistic threats may adopt the same methods. Observed activity included webshells, credential harvesting, mailbox theft and new accounts. Elastic released detection logic on 4 March 2021 and advises patching, Exchange hardening, backups and vulnerability scanning.

db7824ffc792fb6c445b61feef225c2f10f511e7.summary: Hunt & Hackett reports that Sea Turtle, a group it describes as a Turkey-based APT also known as SILICON, ran espionage campaigns in the Netherlands against telecommunication, media, ISP and IT-service providers, including Kurdish-linked targets. Observed activity from 2021 to 2023 used compromised cPanel accounts, SSH access, the SnappyTCP reverse TCP shell and log clearing, and at least one email archive was collected. The attribution to Turkish interests is hedged by the report.

db20ed2a2e346b0a88190bee8a07d123d02a41aa.summary: Trustwave reported a rare BadUSB attack against an unnamed US hospitality provider, in an article dated March 26, 2020. A fake gift card and USB drive were sent; the drive acted as a keyboard and launched a PowerShell download of a JScript-based bot. Facebook and Kaspersky researchers believed a similar file was the work of FIN7. The report also notes a December 2018 Kaspersky case of BadUSB devices found at eight banks in Eastern Europe.

db3e088a3bd7d6d1d9fa03151cbd545d237918f6.summary: Reference page for the BlackMatter malware family, described as ransomware that encrypts files and demands payment for decryption. Encrypted files get a random string appended as an extension, a ransom note is created, and the desktop wallpaper is changed. The page lists vendor and research reports dated 2021 to 2025 about BlackMatter, covering its emergence from DarkSide, its reported shutdown in November 2021, and victims moved to LockBit afterwards. The ransomware description is attributed to PCrisk.
